title: I made a free daily brick breaker that runs inside a Reddit post, where everyone gets the same board
author: gholias
selftext:
Bricks is a daily brick breaker. You drag down anywhere on the board, release, and your balls fly the other way, bouncing around and chipping points off numbered bricks. After every volley the bricks push down a row. If one reaches the rail at the bottom, the attempt is over.

Everyone plays the same board each day: 20 volleys, 3 attempts, and your best score goes on the post's leaderboard. It runs inside the Reddit post, no install, in English, Portuguese and Spanish.

Play today's board: https://www.reddit.com/r/gatuno_games/comments/1x5a3i2/bricks_1_13_oct_2026/

**How it was made**

- **Logo and UI: OpenAI.** I generated the logo and a full phone mockup of the game screen with OpenAI's image model. The colors in the game are sampled straight from the mockup's pixels.
- **GDD: I brainstormed the idea with Fable and use some gameplay references and screenshots to get the final version of the Design Document and Codex reviewed the GDD and approved it before a single line of code was written.
- **Implementation: Claude Fable again.** A browser prototype first, then the Reddit app (Devvit) on the same engine, the translations, the sound, deployment, and the App Review submission.
- **Sound: Kenney.** Every sound effect comes from Kenney's CC0 packs. Nothing generated there.

**What turned out interesting**

- The physics engine is deterministic, so the server replays your inputs and computes the score itself. The client never sends a score, so the leaderboard can't be faked.
- Balance was tuned with two bots: a careless one that breaches around volley 9, and a one-volley look-ahead bot that clears every board. Humans land somewhere in between.


From the first prompt to submitting for Reddit review took about four hours.

Feedback welcome, especially on difficulty. The result screen has a Share button if you want to post your score in the comments.
